query: For a selected high-entropy alloy whose superconducting behavior remains uncharacterized, what governs whether and how superconductivity emerges in the low-temperature test regime, and why? Propose one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison with the starting state, the observations expected relative to that baseline, the limits over which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In a body-centred-cubic (bcc) equiatomic Nb–Ti–Zr–Hf–V high-entropy alloy, the emergence and magnitude of superconductivity at low temperature are governed primarily by the magnitude of local lattice distortion (static micro-strain). Larger distortion enhances the electron–phonon coupling constant λ and therefore raises both the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) and the upper critical field (Hc2). Relief of that distortion by high-temperature annealing will measurably depress Tc and Hc2.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, water-quenched, single-phase bcc (Nb0.2Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2V0.2) alloy containing high frozen-in lattice strain (micro-strain >0.4% from Williamson–Hall analysis).
generation.intervention: Homogenisation anneal at 1000 °C for 24 h in high vacuum followed by slow furnace cooling (≈1 °C min⁻¹) to reduce static micro-strain.
generation.conditions: Low-temperature measurements between 0.3 K and 15 K under magnetic fields μ0H = 0–9 T at ambient pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: Root-mean-square micro-strain (ε_rms) in the bcc lattice, quantified from X-ray diffraction peak broadening.
generation.mechanism: Atomic-size mismatch in the as-cast alloy produces static local lattice distortions that soften selected phonon modes, increasing λ (McMillan–Eliashberg framework). When annealing reduces ε_rms, phonon softening diminishes, lowering λ and thus Tc and Hc2.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed material will exhibit (i) a decrease in Tc by 1 ± 0.5 K, (ii) a ≈10 % lower zero-temperature μ0Hc2, (iii) a smaller heat-capacity jump ΔC/γTc, and (iv) a reduction of ε_rms by ≥30 %.
generation.baseline: Electrical resistivity, magnetisation, and heat-capacity data of the un-annealed (as-cast) alloy measured under identical cryogenic conditions.
generation.boundary: Effect expected for single-phase bcc high-entropy alloys with atomic-size-mismatch parameter 4 % ≤ δ ≤ 8 % and valence-electron concentration 4.3–4.8; not necessarily valid for fcc or hcp HEAs, for δ < 3 %, or under pressures >1 GPa where phonon spectra change substantially.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of Tc shift and precise scaling with ε_rms are uncertain; chemical short-range order, if generated during anneal, could partially counteract the predicted trend.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sample sets: (A) as-cast water-quenched, (B) annealed as described. Measure (1) XRD line broadening to extract ε_rms, (2) temperature-dependent resistivity and magnetisation to obtain Tc and μ0Hc2(T), (3) specific heat to determine ΔC/γTc.
measurements: XRD peak FWHM and Williamson–Hall ε_rms
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed sample shows Tc and μ0Hc2 equal to or higher than the as-cast sample (difference ≤0.1 K for Tc and ≤2 % for μ0Hc2) despite a confirmed ≥30 % reduction in ε_rms, the hypothesis is falsified.
